title: Pointwise flatness criterion on a quasi-finite polynomial chart
statement: Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme; def-weil-affine-spectrum], $f:X\to T$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $U\subseteq X$ an affine open. Let $n\ge0$ and let $e:U\to\mathbb A^n_T$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] be locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], with composition with the projection equal to $f|_U$. For each $x\in U$, the local-ring map induced by $e$ at $x$ is flat if and only if the depth of the fibre local ring of $f$ at $x$ equals its ring Krull dimension and the topological Krull dimension of that fibre at $x$ equals $n$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk; def-weil-pbc-depth; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring; def-pc-scheme-fibre; def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point].

source.place: Tags 00RE and 00R7, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00RE and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00R7; pointwise argument in Tag 00RH, with Tag 00N8; read 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Apply the geometric local-algebra comparison to obtain a regular local source R, a local map phi to the actual fibre stalk S, and finite dimensions d and r with a shared residue transcendence degree t. It identifies original stalk flatness with phi-flatness, gives closed-fibre dimension zero and r<=d, and gives fibre dimension r+t and n=d+t.

Prove depth(R)=d directly in Lean. Choose a minimal finite generating set of its maximal ideal, turn it into a regular system of parameters of length d, and use the regular-generators theorem. Its regular sequence witnesses depth at least d by the definition of depth. The depth-support dimension bound for R over itself gives the opposite inequality.

In the forward direction, phi is flat local, hence faithfully flat, so d<=r. Together with r<=d this gives r=d and thus fibre dimension n. The flat local depth formula provides a local structure on the closed fibre and computes depth(S) as depth(R)+depth(closed fibre). The depth-support dimension bound on that nonzero closed fibre of dimension zero gives depth zero. Hence depth(S)=d=dim(S). All comparisons and arithmetic are written in Lean.

In the reverse direction, fibre dimension n means r+t=d+t and therefore r=d by natural-number cancellation. The given depth equality supplies depth(S)>=r. Since the closed fibre has dimension zero, dim(S)=dim(R)+dim(closed fibre). Apply miracle flatness to phi and transport flatness back using the geometric comparison.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00RE and 00R7 as used in 00RH. The geometric comparison is split into lem-sbc-polynomial-chart-local-algebra; the regular-depth, closed-fibre-depth, faithful-flat dimension and miracle-flatness combination is fully written in Lean by C4.

lean.statement:
theorem polynomial_chart_flat_stalk_iff_fibre_depth_and_dimension
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] (f : X ⟶ T)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (U : X.Opens) [IsAffine U.toScheme] (n : ℕ)
    (e : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation e] [LocallyQuasiFinite e]
    (he : e ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T ↘ T) = U.ι ≫ f)
    (x : U.toScheme) :
    (e.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ↔
      (IsLocalRing.depth
          (R := (f.fiber (f (U.ι x))).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber (U.ι x)))
          ((f.fiber (f (U.ι x))).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber (U.ι x))) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
        ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (f (U.ι x))).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber (U.ι x))) ∧
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber (U.ι x)) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)
